title: Create an ext4 file system on a partition
summary: Format a partition with the ext4 file system, which is the standard choice for Linux data partitions. This erases all existing data on the target partition.
prerequisites: You have backed up any data you want to keep on this partition.

steps.explain: Identify the device name of the partition you want to format (e.g., /dev/sda1).
Unmount the partition if it is currently mounted.

placeholders.name: DEVICE
placeholders.description: The device path of the partition, e.g., /dev/sda1

steps.explain: Create a new ext4 file system on the specified partition. This destroys all existing data on the partition.

placeholders.name: DEVICE
placeholders.description: The device path of the partition, e.g., /dev/sda1

verify.expect: The FSTYPE column for the target device shows 'ext4'.

rollback.explain: Data recovery after formatting is difficult and not guaranteed. Restore from a backup if available.

warnings: Formatting a partition erases all data on it. Ensure you have selected the correct device.
Do not format a partition that is currently in use or mounted.
